nehemiah.4.p1.b1.text: Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and filled with indignation. He ridiculed the Jews …

nehemiah.4.p1.b2.text: “What are these feeble Jews doing? … Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the mounds of rubble?”

nehemiah.4.p1.b3.text: “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”

nehemiah.4.p2.b1.text: Hear us, O God, for we are despised.

nehemiah.4.p2.b2.text: So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height …

nehemiah.4.p2.b3.text: … for the people had a mind to work.

nehemiah.4.p3.b1.text: When Sanballat and Tobiah, together with the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites, heard that the repair to the walls of Jerusalem was progressing … they were furious

nehemiah.4.p3.b2.text: and all of them conspired to come and fight against Jerusalem and create a hindrance.

nehemiah.4.p3.b3.text: So we prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.

nehemiah.4.p4.b1.text: “The strength of the laborer fails, and there is so much rubble that we will never be able to rebuild the wall.”

nehemiah.4.p4.b2.text: “Before they know or see a thing, we will come into their midst, kill them, and put an end to the work.”

nehemiah.4.p4.b3.text: At that time the Jews who lived nearby came and told us ten times over

nehemiah.4.p4.b4.text: “Wherever you turn, they will attack us.”

nehemiah.4.p5.b1.text: So I stationed men behind the lowest sections of the wall, at the vulnerable areas. I stationed them by families with their swords, spears, and bows.

nehemiah.4.p5.b2.text: After I had made an inspection, I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people

nehemiah.4.p5.b4.text: Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your homes.”

nehemiah.4.p6.b1.text: When our enemies heard that we were aware of their scheme and that God had frustrated it, each of us returned to his own work on the wall.

nehemiah.4.p6.b2.text: … who were rebuilding the wall. The laborers who carried materials worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.

nehemiah.4.p6.b3.text: And each of the builders worked with his sword strapped at his side …

nehemiah.4.p6.b4.text: … But the trumpeter stayed beside me.

nehemiah.4.p7.b1.text: “The work is great and extensive, and we are spread out far from one another along the wall.

nehemiah.4.p7.b2.text: Wherever you hear the sound of the horn, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us!”

nehemiah.4.p7.b3.text: So we continued the work, while half of the men held spears from the break of dawn until the stars came out.

nehemiah.4.p7.b4.text: So neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the guards with me changed out of our clothes; each carried his weapon, even to go for water.
